children: will be reporting earnings this Monday after market hours. Here’s what you need to know.

Simpson beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $671.1 million, up 6.3% year on year. It was an exceptional quarter for the company, with an impressive beat of analysts’ EBITDA estimates and a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates.
Is Simpson a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Simpson’s revenue to be flat year on year, slowing from the 6.2% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Simpson rarely misses Wall Street’s revenue estimates.

Looking at Simpson’s peers in the building products segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Apogee delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 9.2%, beating analysts’ expectations by 11.3%, and AZZ reported revenues up 16.7%, topping estimates by 5.1%. Apogee traded up 15.3% following the results while AZZ’s stock price was unchanged.

In the last twelve months or so, the market has shifted its attention from one area of macro importance to the next (AI disintermediation and AI capex spending to geopolitical conflict, rates, and whether the economy is on solid footing or not). While some of the building products stocks have shown solid performance in this choppy environment, the group has generally underperformed, with share prices down 6% on average over the last month. Simpson is up 4.5% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $216 (compared to the current share price of $184.51).
